notes:
Lead source: inbound signup (self-serve). Small SaaS that adds chat + tool integrations to their app. Primary contact is CTO (Evan Liu).

Summary of issue (customer words / logs):
- Using hosted API, streaming=true, mode=\"json\" (attempting structured output + function calling).
- Client receives multiple stream chunks which are not valid JSON when concatenated due to trailing newlines and partial escapes; front-end JSON.parse fails on the assembled payload.
- When calling functions, the agent returns a function_call with arguments stringified (escaped JSON) rather than a parsed object; their client expects a JS object. Example: function_call.arguments = \"{\"id\": \"123\", \"items\": \"[1,2]\"}\" -> items typed as string.
- Observed repeated re-parsing errors in browser console: \"Unexpected token \" in JSON at position 0\" and also \"TypeError: arguments is not an object\".
- Tried toggling streaming back off (non-streaming responses parse fine) which points to difference in chunk handling.

They've tried:
- Using our SDK (node) and a homegrown fetch-based client. Both show chunk boundaries cutting across JSON tokens.
- Wrapping client to buffer full event stream until \"data: [DONE]\" then parse -> works but defeats streaming low-latency requirement.
- Attempted server-side reassembly using newline-delimited JSON heuristics; brittle.

Customer constraints and targets:
- Latency target: p95 token latency ~300ms.
- Low throughput (few rps), cost sensitive.
- Wants streaming for perceived improved UX and progressive rendering.
- Wants built-in function calling for backend tool invocation (DB lookups, external API).

Quotes from call: \"We need an example that shows streaming + function schema that we can drop into our frontend. Right now chunks arrive malformed and our parser chokes.\"

Suggested immediate responses from AE/SE:
- Provide a minimal server + client repro (node fetch + plain websocket example) showing recommended parsing pattern (process newline-prefixed event stream; accumulate partial JSON tokens; use official SDK streaming helpers where available).
- Explain differences between event-stream framing and RFC-8259 streaming approaches and recommended client-side strategy.
- Verify content-type and transfer-encoding headers in their requests (they saw occasional missing chunk delimiters from 3rd-party proxy).

Priority: medium. Customer is in early discovery but likely to convert to self-serve hosted customers if UX fixed quickly.

Stubs/links: Drive deck with pricing + example code, Fireflies transcript ff_2026_02_25_321, support ticket INFR-3421.
